To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SBS symptoms are associated to personality factors that create a vulnerability for SBS, and that the SBS symptoms are maintained by psychological factors such as anxiety and hyperventalilation.
SBS patients have personality traits within a normal range and that poor psychological work environments are associated to SBS.
SBS patients can be treated successfully with a combination of cognitive behavioral therapy and environmental medicine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the SBS symptoms and how they are generated and treated.
the SBS symptoms, the psychosocial factors, and the treatment of SBS patients with the Integrative Model for Environmental Illness of Psychogenic Nature (IMEI).
the development of a treatment model for SBS patients and to test the model in a clinical setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SBS is not an illness of a physical nature.
SBS symptoms are a result of an environmental illness of psychogenic nature, that is treatable with a focus on uncovering and treating environmental sensitivity of a psycho-genic nature.
SBS is not a disease but a symptom complex of psychogenic nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SBS patients can be treated effectively and successfully with a treatment method that is based on the understanding of the psychogenic nature of the symptoms and on a broad understanding of the field of environmental health and medicine.
the SBS patients are not hysterics, but they suffer from environmental illnesses of psychogenic nature.
SBS symptoms are not a result of physical exposures but are a result of a psychological process of generating anxiety and hypervigilance to the environment.

the SBS is an illness with a psychogenic background.
the SBS symptoms are not caused by the physical environment.
